target_customer: Startups and developers who need live paid help from expert programmers
problem: Developers get stuck on specific stacks and need an expert on screen share faster than hiring or forum answers.
business_model: Marketplace taking a cut of paid expert sessions by the hour

founders.name: Jonathon Kresner
previous_startups: Online rock climbing partner site launched in London in 2008
founders.background_notes: Background from Wikipedia as quoted in search results, not opened.

competitors.name: Codementor
competitors.what: Marketplace for one on one programming help, priced in 15 minute blocks
competitors.traction_then: Opened to the public in March 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace with scheduling, payments and video or screen sharing built on existing tools.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided expert network gave mild liquidity advantage but competitors launched the same year.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source on incumbent copying; Wikipedia talk page claims a 2015 dissolution, unverified.

market_need_then: Kresner reported ramen profitability in November 2013 per Wikipedia, and the company partnered with Stripe and Twilio in 2014 for API help.

branding.name_origin: Founder said the concept comes from the British English word upskill, per Network World.
branding.domain_note: Company site listed as airpair.com per Wikipedia.

brand_strength.rationale: Some press and a widely read bootstrapping blog post, but no mascot or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: AirPair bootstrapped to ramen profitability, joined YC Winter 2014 and raised about one million dollars within days of demo day. Competitors such as Codementor launched the same spring. An unsourced Wikipedia talk page note says it dissolved in 2015, so the cause of the end is not public and the competition factor is an inference to verify.
notes: Funding: CB Insights lists Seed VC rounds dated 2014-01-26 (amount not shown, total about 1.02M implies roughly 20K, not stated) and 2014-04-10 (1M); Xconomy dates an undisclosed seed 2014-03-26. The 1M figure rests on CB Insights plus Wellfound, both databases. Website returned HTTP 503. Competitor HackHands is named in Wikipedia and TechCrunch but its date was not seen, so omitted. Shutdown date and cause unverified; failure_factors competition_won is tentative.
